Address Form asks for an address the way the shopper’s country writes it. A US address gets City, State and ZIP code on one row, the UK gets Town or city and Postcode with no state, Germany puts the postal code before the city, and Japan starts with the postal code and prefecture. Sixteen countries have their own format with labels, required fields, region lists and postal rules, and every other country gets a plain fallback.

Errors show when you leave a field, then update as you type until it’s fixed, and they say what’s wrong: “Enter a 5-digit ZIP code”, “Enter a postcode like SW1A 1AA”. validate() lists every problem in a summary at the top with links to the fields and moves focus there. Switching country keeps what still fits, clears regions that don’t, and re-checks only fields you’ve already visited, while the form’s height animates to the new layout.
Every field has a visible label, and optional fields say Optional. Errors are linked with aria-invalid and aria-describedby and use text next to the red outline, never color alone.

onSearchAddress returns suggestions for what’s typed and onResolveAddress turns the picked one into an Address. The same two calls map onto Mapbox Search Box’s /suggest and /retrieve. Both get an AbortSignal, so stale requests are cancelled.
validate() moves focus to a summary titled There is a problem. Each item is a link worded like the inline error that focuses its field.

validate() returns the errors and focuses the summary, so saving only runs on a complete address. The Address maps to customerAddressCreate field by field, and a userError from Shopify shows under the form.
validate() returns { field, message }[] and shows the summary, focus(field), setCountry(code) and reset(address).
